headline: Imported oranges costing 87 taka sold for 520 taka per kg in retail markets
summary: A staggering 121.78% import duty and a surge in demand due to the dengue outbreak are identified as key factors driving the price of imported oranges up by over five times their import cost.
details: Imported oranges from South Africa and Egypt, costing approximately 87 Taka per kg to bring into Bangladesh, are now being sold for 480-520 Taka per kg in Chittagong's retail markets. This represents a more than five-fold increase from the import price to the consumer.

An analysis by Prothom Alo reveals that a significant portion of this price hike occurs at the import stage due to a total customs duty of 121.78%. Additional costs include transportation and other ancillary expenses.

According to Bangladesh Customs, the total tax burden on fresh fruits like oranges and mandarins is 121.78%, encompassing import duty, regulatory duty, supplementary duty, VAT, and advance income tax. This means that after customs clearance, the cost per kg already stands at 193-194 Taka.

Businesses report that further costs of 10-15 Taka per kg are added for refrigerated container handling, transport from port to warehouse, and other associated expenses. Importers claim that factoring in spoilage and other port-related costs, their actual expense reaches 230-240 Taka per kg.

After clearance, oranges move to wholesale markets in Chittagong and Dhaka, with prices fluctuating based on demand and supply at each stage. Chittagong's fruit market traders noted that wholesale prices rapidly increased from 220-230 Taka per kg three weeks ago to 400-500 Taka per kg.

Retail markets in Chittagong sold oranges for 480-520 Taka per kg last Wednesday. Fruit trader Md. Babul stated that reduced imports due to previous losses by importers from June to August, combined with increased demand in September, led to the rapid price hike.

The demand surge is significantly linked to the increased incidence of dengue fever. As of September 30, 79,620 people were hospitalized and 245 died from dengue this year, with a rapid increase in cases and deaths in September. Families of dengue patients are buying more oranges and similar fruits, further driving up demand.

The National Directorate of Consumer Rights Protection in Chittagong has taken notice, conducting raids and fining three establishments 13,000 Taka in the fruit market. They stated that their operations will continue.

The high tax burden on imported fruits is a recent development. In 2021-22, the total tax on oranges was around 89%. To discourage imports amidst the dollar crisis, a 20% regulatory duty was imposed in May 2022, further increasing the tax burden.

headline_marked: [[Petrobangla announces large recruitment]] for 753 posts in grades 9 & 10
headline: Petrobangla announces large recruitment for 753 posts in grades 9 & 10
summary: Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Resources Corporation (Petrobangla) has issued a recruitment circular for 753 positions in grades 9 and 10. These roles are available across Petrobangla and its 12 subsidiary companies.
details: Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Resources Corporation (Petrobangla) has published a recruitment circular for 753 positions in grades 9 and 10. These opportunities are available across Petrobangla and its 12 subsidiary companies, offering a significant boost to employment in the energy sector.

Grade 9 positions include Assistant Manager roles in Administration (97), Law (6), Finance (63), Engineering (various disciplines like Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, CSE/IT, Chemical, Petroleum, etc., totaling 227), Geology (12), Geophysics (2), Geochemical (1), Chemistry (1), Environment (1), Medical (15), and Technical (11). There is also one Assistant Dealer position.

Grade 10 positions encompass Assistant Officer roles in Administration (73), Law (4), and Finance (53), along with Sub-Assistant Engineer roles in various engineering fields (Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Computer/IT, Electronics, Automobile, Chemical, Power, Telecom, totaling 150). Other roles include Assistant Librarian (1), Trainee Dealer (4), and Assistant Technical Officer (11).

The salary scale for Grade 9 positions (posts 1-12) ranges from BDT 44,000 to BDT 105,900. For Grade 10 positions (posts 13-19), the salary scale is BDT 32,000 to BDT 77,300, providing competitive compensation for successful candidates.

Applicants must be aged 32 years or below as of October 1, 2026. Applications must be submitted online through bogmc.teletalk.com.bd, with a general application fee of BDT 223. Candidates from underprivileged groups (ethnic minorities, physically challenged, and third gender) pay a reduced fee of BDT 56.

The application process begins on October 18, 2026, at 10:00 AM, and the deadline for submitting applications and fees is November 17, 2026, at 5:00 PM. Candidates who receive a user ID can submit their fees for an additional 72 hours, until November 20, 2026, at 5:00 PM.
